source.title: Visualising Basins of Attraction for the Cross-Entropy and the Squared Error Neural Network Loss Functions
source.authors: Anna Sergeevna Bosman; A. Engelbrecht; Mardé Helbig

record.tranche_reason: Measures training and test classification error on natural datasets along progressive gradient walks, but does not test any version's specified intervention or setup.
record.gate_note: Reports aggregate classification errors at the last step of gradient walks; they are not results from standard training recipes. Rows record these train/test error pairs. The paper also reports cited prior findings, which are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study compares squared-error and cross-entropy loss landscapes using progressive gradient walks through single-hidden-layer sigmoid networks. Its own results do not test V1–V8. In particular, gradients and inferred valley widths do not measure V7's magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance or its ranking of generalization gaps. The different sampling recipe alone is not grounds for exclusion; the missing claim-specific comparisons and measures are.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the generalization conclusion. The authors report that cross-entropy has stronger gradients, fewer stationary attractors and a more searchable landscape; squared error is less prone to overfitting in some settings. They associate continued descent within valleys with deteriorating generalization on most problems and hypothesize that wide valleys generalize better. These are conclusions from progressive gradient samples; the statement that this is not a standard-training comparison is an assessment of the experimental design, rather than an explicit author qualification.
record.recipe_differences: Progressive gradient walks sampled loss surfaces; not standard model training or the specified version recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, loss (SSE or CE), initialization range ([−1, 1] or [−10, 10]), and walk granularity (micro or macro) vary.

fits_no_version.finding: Final-step training and test classification scores differ across losses, datasets, initialization ranges and walk granularities.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Squared-error and cross-entropy losses can yield different held-out classification performance under progressive gradient sampling of sigmoid-network weight spaces.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors associate lower-gradient, inferred wide valleys with better test loss in selected comparisons and report stronger overfitting near some cross-entropy minima. Valley width is inferred from loss-gradient clouds rather than measured through magnitude-scaled weight perturbations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Loss-gradient structure can accompany differences in test loss along progressive gradient walks through single-hidden-layer sigmoid networks.

record.problems: The reported classification errors are averages across gradient walks and do not establish performance under standard gradient training recipes. No controls are reported for these results.
record.rows_left_out: None; all classification-error aggregates in Appendix B, Tables B.10–B.15 are included.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe; random-label held-out performance.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, including tuning, weight decay and optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps among similarly fitted convolutional networks, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removal of highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All rows retain versions ['none']: endpoint classification scores alone do not measure any listed version. Shared Ct/Cg issue: Appendix B calls these quantities classification errors, but the conclusion interprets values approaching 1 as approaching 100% accuracy. Dataset discussions also generally treat higher Cg as better. Preserve the reported numbers while flagging the apparent accuracy/error naming inconsistency; do not interpret values near 1 as near-total misclassification. Et/Eg are loss values and must be distinguished from Ct/Cg classification scores. The rows summarize final steps across walks, not verified converged optima. No omitted result directly testing V1–V8 was identified.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same standard training recipe.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation on MNIST or CIFAR-10.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.
